description: Hi! I’m Sara, the team leader of Ares Nebula. I’m passionate about astrophysics, space exploration, Mars, and cosmology. We are looking for motivated teammates interested in astrophysics, programming, AI, data science, or web development. Let’s build a creative project for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.
summary:
NASA's SPHEREx mission generates vast amounts of astronomical data, capturing celestial objects across multiple infrared wavelengths and observation dates. However, accessing, processing and interpreting this data can be challenging, particularly for students, citizen scientists and researchers without specialised astronomy tools.

Ares Nebula simplifies astronomical exploration by allowing users to search for observations using celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), dynamically retrieve FITS files and visualise objects across different wavelengths and time periods. By combining automated data retrieval, astronomical coordinate processing and scientific visualisation, our solution makes complex NASA datasets more accessible and easier to investigate.

Infrared astronomy provides valuable insights into celestial objects that may be difficult to observe using visible light alone. Our project enables users to compare observations, investigate unusual infrared sources and explore potential changes or movement in the sky. It also establishes a foundation for future AI-driven anomaly detection and candidate classification.

Ultimately, SphereX-Ares bridges the gap between NASA's scientific data and public exploration, supporting citizen science, encouraging astronomical discovery and enabling more people to participate in understanding our universe.
details:
Ares Nebula

Our project is an astronomical data ingestion, visualisation, and analysis platform built around NASA's SPHEREx mission. Our initial scientific target is WISE 0855, an extremely cold brown dwarf with significant proper motion. The platform dynamically retrieves infrared observations from NASA/IPAC's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), processes FITS images, and enables users to investigate astronomical objects across different observation dates and wavelengths.

Data Retrieval and Processing

The Python backend connects to IRSA using the IVOA Simple Image Access 2.0 protocol, supporting SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 observations. Users can search using Right Ascension, Declination, search radius, date range, and exposure count.

Observation metadata includes timestamps, wavelengths, detector information, spatial coverage, and FITS download locations. Rather than downloading entire survey images, the application retrieves smaller, targeted FITS cutouts, reducing processing time and data transfer.

Downloads are validated, securely stored, and tracked using metadata manifests and SHA-256 checksums to ensure reproducibility and data integrity.

Astrometry and Scientific Analysis

A central capability is tracking astronomical objects that change position over time. Using Astropy, the platform accounts for proper motion and annual parallax, propagating an object's expected position to each observation date.

The scientific processing pipeline handles SPHEREx FITS products containing image data, variance, quality flags, point-spread functions, and wavelength calibration. World Coordinate System (WCS) transformations identify celestial positions within detector images.

The system supports target-centred image extraction, quality assessment, wavelength estimation, and aperture-based measurements with uncertainty calculations. Potential detections are treated as exploratory evidence rather than confirmed astronomical discoveries.

Interactive Visualisation

Our React and TypeScript web application provides an interactive environment for exploring SPHEREx observations.

Users can compare multiple observation epochs using temporal astrometry, blink between images, generate difference images, and examine changes in brightness or apparent position.

A candidate investigation tool measures source centroids across observations to identify potential movement, while accounting for uncertainties caused by image resolution, wavelength differences, and overlapping sources.

Hyperspectral visualisation enables users to explore different infrared wavelengths, create false-colour composites, and examine sampled spectral-energy distributions.

Architecture and Reliability

The platform combines a Python scientific-processing backend, HTTP API, React/TypeScript web portal, command-line tools, and a Tkinter desktop viewer.

Scientific Impact

Our solution makes SPHEREx observations more accessible to students, citizen scientists, and researchers
